title: Milestone: Fuel and Oxygen
objective: After this level you can connect digestion, breathing and blood into one picture of how cells get energy.
summary: Digestion turns lunch into glucose, the blood carries it past the liver to every cell, and mitochondria combine it with oxygen from the lungs to release its energy.

cards.headline: Milestone: halfway to Mastery. Follow one bite all the way to a cell.
cards.body: You've taken food down the tube, through the stomach and intestines, and past the liver. One question is left: where does the energy in your lunch actually get used? The answer is inside your cells.

cards.headline: From lunch to a power station
cards.body: Digestion breaks the starch in your lunch into simple sugars, and your body turns them into glucose, your cells' main fuel. The small intestine absorbs it, and your blood takes it to the liver first, then on to cells all over your body. Inside each cell, Level 2's mitochondria convert the energy from food into a form the cell can use. Fuel you don't need right away can be stored in the liver, muscles and body fat.

cards.headline: Fuel meets oxygen
cards.body: Mitochondria can't release that energy from fuel alone. In cellular respiration, cells combine oxygen with food molecules to free their chemical energy. That oxygen comes from your lungs into your blood, and your cardiovascular system carries it, along with the nutrients, to the tissues: Level 1's teamwork again. Breakfast and breath end up in the same tiny place.

mascot.line: Level 31's breathing and this chapter's digestion meet here, in the same tiny place.

cards.headline: Milestone: fuel delivered
learned: How a bite of food becomes energy: pushed along one tube, absorbed, then burned with oxygen in cells.
Why the small intestine's folded lining lets it absorb almost all your nutrients.
How the liver processes what you absorb and the kidneys filter your blood, then take most of it back.
Why a lack of vitamin C causes scurvy, and why the cure took decades to catch on.

questions.prompt: Food and Digestion milestone: in what order does food pass through the digestive tract?

options.label: Mouth, stomach, esophagus, large intestine, small intestine
options.rationale: The esophagus comes before the stomach.

options.label: Mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
Mouth, esophagus, small intestine, stomach, large intestine
options.rationale: The stomach comes before the small intestine.

options.label: Mouth, liver, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
options.rationale: The liver sits beside the tube.

questions.explanation: The tube runs mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, anus.

questions.prompt: Food and Digestion milestone: what is the hardest substance in the human body?

options.label: Thigh bone
options.rationale: Bone is hard, but enamel is harder.

questions.explanation: Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the body, about 95 percent mineral.

questions.prompt: Food and Digestion milestone: about what share of the fluid your kidneys filter goes back into your blood?

options.label: About 1 percent
options.rationale: That's roughly the share that becomes urine.

questions.explanation: Of 150 to 180 liters filtered a day, about 99 percent returns to the blood and 1 to 2 liters become urine.

questions.prompt: Food and Digestion milestone: why does a lack of vitamin C lead to bleeding gums and wounds that won't heal?

options.label: Vitamin C is the body's main fuel
The body can't make collagen properly

questions.explanation: Vitamin C is needed to make collagen, so without it connective tissue weakens.

questions.prompt: Food and Digestion milestone: glucose from your lunch reaches a muscle cell. What happens to its energy there?

options.label: It is stored in the nucleus as DNA
It is turned back into starch in the blood
options.rationale: Starch is broken down, not rebuilt, in the blood.

options.label: Mitochondria convert it into a form the cell can use

questions.explanation: Mitochondria convert the energy from food into a form the cell can use.

questions.prompt: Food and Digestion milestone: which organ system delivers both absorbed nutrients and oxygen to your cells?

options.label: The digestive system
options.rationale: It absorbs nutrients but doesn't deliver them.

options.label: The urinary system
options.rationale: It filters waste from the blood.

questions.explanation: The cardiovascular system carries oxygen from the lungs and nutrients from the gut to the tissues.

questions.prompt: Food and Digestion milestone: Level 7 said water is 50 to 60 percent of an adult. Which part of the digestive tract takes water back from the leftovers?

options.label: The stomach
options.rationale: Water is taken back later, in the large intestine.

questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs water and turns what's left into stool.
